parameters.name: Patch Compliance Rate
parameters.definition: % of Windows systems with all required patches applied within SLA windows at any given point in time.

rubric.level1: No formal patching. Compliance unknown. Patches applied only after incidents.
rubric.level2: Patching occurs inconsistently. Manually tracked. <70% compliance. Significant gaps.
rubric.level3: Documented patch schedule. Tooling used (WSUS/SCCM/Intune). 70-89% compliance.
rubric.level4: Automated deployment with exception management. 90-95% compliance. SLA breaches escalated.
rubric.level5: Zero-touch automated patching. >95% compliance. Integrated with vulnerability management. Real-time dashboards.

parameters.name: Mean Time to Patch (MTTP)
parameters.definition: Average elapsed time from patch release by Microsoft to successful deployment across the estate, measured by severity tier.

rubric.level1: No SLA defined. Patches applied weeks or months after release, if ever.
rubric.level2: Informal SLA rarely met. Critical patches take >30 days. No severity tiering.
rubric.level3: SLA defined by severity (Critical 14 days, High 30 days). Tracked but not always met.
rubric.level4: SLA consistently met: Critical 7 days, High 14 days, Medium 30 days. Exceptions tracked.
rubric.level5: Critical patches deployed within 72 hours. Automated pipeline with pre-tested packages. Real-time SLA reporting.

parameters.name: Failed Patch Deployment Rate
parameters.definition: % of patch attempts that fail and require manual intervention or re-execution before compliance is achieved.

rubric.level1: Failures not tracked. Patching done manually with no visibility into success or failure.
rubric.level2: Some failures logged but no root cause analysis. Failure rate >15%. Remediation is reactive.
rubric.level3: Failures tracked in patching tool. Rate between 5-15%. Basic retry logic exists.
rubric.level4: Failure rate <5%. Root cause analysis performed. Automated retry and remediation workflows.
rubric.level5: Failure rate <1%. Pre-deployment staging tests. Self-healing remediation scripts. Continuous improvement of package quality.

parameters.name: CIS Benchmark Compliance Score
parameters.definition: % of CIS Windows Benchmark controls passing across the managed estate, assessed via automated scanning tools such as Nessus, Qualys, or Microsoft Secure Score.

rubric.level1: No awareness or application of CIS benchmarks. No hardening baseline defined.
rubric.level2: Ad hoc hardening applied. No formal benchmark adopted. Score below 50%.
rubric.level3: CIS benchmark adopted. Automated scanning in place. Score between 50-75%.
rubric.level4: Score between 75-90%. Exceptions documented with risk acceptance. Remediation tracked.
rubric.level5: Score above 90% consistently. Benchmark enforced in golden image. Continuous compliance drift detection.

parameters.name: Endpoint Protection Coverage
parameters.definition: % of Windows endpoints with an active, up-to-date endpoint protection or EDR solution deployed and reporting telemetry.

rubric.level1: No centralised endpoint protection. Antivirus deployed ad hoc or not at all.
rubric.level2: Antivirus deployed on most systems but not centrally managed. Gaps exist. No EDR.
rubric.level3: Centralised AV/EPP deployed on more than 90% of estate. Managed console with reporting.
rubric.level4: EDR deployed across more than 95% of estate. Alerts integrated with SIEM. Automated response.
rubric.level5: 100% EDR coverage. AI-driven threat detection. Automated containment. Zero blind spots.

parameters.name: BitLocker Encryption Coverage
parameters.definition: % of Windows endpoints with full-disk encryption enforced via BitLocker, with recovery keys escrowed centrally.

rubric.level1: No encryption enforced. No policy in place.
rubric.level2: BitLocker enabled on some devices. No central key escrow. Inconsistent enforcement.
rubric.level3: BitLocker enforced via GPO on more than 80% of endpoints. Keys stored in AD or Intune.
rubric.level4: 100% encryption on all portable devices. Keys centrally managed. Compliance reporting automated.
rubric.level5: 100% coverage including desktops. Pre-boot authentication enforced. Key rotation automated. Audit-ready.

parameters.name: LAPS Deployment Rate
parameters.definition: % of Windows systems using Microsoft Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) to manage and rotate unique local admin passwords per device.

rubric.level1: Shared or static local admin passwords in use across the estate.
rubric.level2: LAPS deployed on some systems. Large portions still using shared passwords.
rubric.level3: LAPS deployed on more than 70% of estate. Policy defined. Some manual password management remains.
rubric.level4: LAPS deployed on more than 95% of estate. Automated rotation. Integrated with PAM solution.
rubric.level5: 100% LAPS coverage. Integrated with enterprise PAM. Automated audit and anomaly detection.

parameters.name: Stale Account Ratio
parameters.definition: % of Active Directory accounts inactive for more than 90 days that have not been reviewed, disabled, or removed.

rubric.level1: No account lifecycle process. Stale accounts accumulate indefinitely. No review performed.
rubric.level2: Periodic manual reviews occur. More than 15% of accounts are stale. No automation.
rubric.level3: Quarterly reviews scheduled. Stale accounts below 10%. Semi-automated discovery in place.
rubric.level4: Automated stale account detection. Below 5% stale. Monthly review cycle with auto-disable.
rubric.level5: Below 1% stale accounts. Automated lifecycle management. Joiners, movers, leavers fully automated.

parameters.name: MFA Enforcement Coverage
parameters.definition: % of user accounts for which multi-factor authentication is enforced for all access to Windows systems and management planes.

rubric.level1: No MFA enforced. Password-only authentication across all systems.
rubric.level2: MFA available but optional. Adopted by less than 50% of users. Privileged accounts unprotected.
rubric.level3: MFA enforced for all privileged accounts and remote access. Regular users partially covered.
rubric.level4: MFA enforced for more than 95% of all accounts. Conditional Access policies in place.
rubric.level5: 100% MFA with phishing-resistant methods such as FIDO2 or Windows Hello. Zero exceptions.

parameters.name: GPO Compliance Rate
parameters.definition: % of Active Directory Group Policy Objects applied as intended, with no configuration drift between defined policy and actual system state.

rubric.level1: GPOs exist but are not managed or audited. Significant drift and conflicts present.
rubric.level2: GPOs defined but poorly documented. Drift not detected. Manual audits rarely performed.
rubric.level3: GPO structure documented. Quarterly compliance checks. Drift detected via tooling.
rubric.level4: GPO compliance above 90%. Automated drift detection with alerting. Changes tracked in change management.
rubric.level5: GPO compliance above 98%. All changes via approved pipeline. Drift auto-remediated. Full audit trail.

parameters.name: System Uptime and Availability
parameters.definition: % of scheduled uptime during which Windows systems are available and fully operational, excluding planned maintenance windows.

rubric.level1: No uptime tracking. Availability unknown. Outages managed entirely reactively.
rubric.level2: Basic uptime monitoring via ping. Availability approximately 95%. No SLA defined.
rubric.level3: Agent-based monitoring deployed. Availability tracked against SLA. Targeting 99%.
rubric.level4: 99.5% availability achieved. Automated alerting and escalation. Capacity planning in place.
rubric.level5: 99.9% or higher availability. Predictive failure detection. Automated failover. Zero unplanned outages per quarter.

parameters.name: Event Log Monitoring Coverage
parameters.definition: % of Windows systems whose security, application, and system event logs are centrally collected, parsed, and alerted on in real time.

rubric.level1: No centralised log collection. Logs reviewed only after incidents occur.
rubric.level2: Logs collected from some systems to a central store. No real-time alerting.
rubric.level3: More than 80% of systems sending logs to SIEM. Basic alert rules defined. Reviewed regularly.
rubric.level4: More than 95% log coverage. Correlated alerts. Automated triage for common events.
rubric.level5: 100% coverage. AI-driven anomaly detection. Automated response playbooks. SOC-integrated.

parameters.name: EOL OS Exposure Rate
parameters.definition: % of Windows systems running OS versions that have reached End-of-Life and no longer receive security updates from Microsoft.

rubric.level1: No lifecycle tracking. Significant EOL OS in production such as Windows Server 2008 or Windows 7.
rubric.level2: EOL systems identified but no formal remediation plan. More than 20% of estate on EOL OS.
rubric.level3: EOL inventory maintained. Remediation plan in place. Between 5-20% of estate on EOL OS.
rubric.level4: Below 5% EOL OS. Upgrade projects tracked. ESU licensing managed where unavoidable.
rubric.level5: Zero EOL OS in production. Lifecycle roadmap proactively managed. OS upgrades automated.

parameters.name: Golden Image Currency
parameters.definition: Age and patch state of the base OS image used for provisioning new Windows systems, measured by time since last update.

rubric.level1: No golden image. Systems built manually each time. No standardisation.
rubric.level2: Golden image exists but updated infrequently, more than 6 months old. Manual build process.
rubric.level3: Golden image updated quarterly. Includes current patches. Stored in image library.
rubric.level4: Golden image updated monthly. Automated build pipeline. Validation tests run before release.
rubric.level5: Golden image updated with every patch cycle. Fully automated build, test, and release pipeline. Zero manual steps.

parameters.name: Automated Provisioning Coverage
parameters.definition: % of new Windows system builds delivered via automated provisioning tools such as MDT, SCCM, Intune Autopilot, or Ansible, versus manual installation.

rubric.level1: All systems built manually. No automation. Build time exceeds 4 hours per system.
rubric.level2: Automation tools available but used inconsistently. Less than 50% of builds automated.
rubric.level3: Between 50-80% of builds automated. Standard process defined. Build time under 2 hours.
rubric.level4: More than 90% automated provisioning. Build time under 45 minutes. Self-service for standard builds.
rubric.level5: 100% automated provisioning. Zero-touch deployment. Build time under 15 minutes. Full auditability.

parameters.name: Backup Success Rate
parameters.definition: % of scheduled backup jobs for Windows systems that complete successfully without error within the defined backup window.

rubric.level1: No formalised backups. Data loss risk is high. Backups done ad hoc if at all.
rubric.level2: Backups configured but not monitored. Success rate below 85%. Recovery never tested.
rubric.level3: Backups monitored. Success rate between 85-95%. Recovery tested annually.
rubric.level4: Success rate above 98%. Failures trigger automated alerts and retries. Recovery tested quarterly.
rubric.level5: Above 99.5% success rate. Automated recovery testing. RTOs and RPOs validated continuously. Immutable backups.

parameters.name: Configuration Drift Detection
parameters.definition: The ability to detect when a Windows system's actual configuration deviates from its approved baseline, and the speed of remediation.

rubric.level1: No baseline defined. Configuration drift is unknown and undetected.
rubric.level2: Baseline documented but drift not actively monitored. Manual periodic audits only.
rubric.level3: Drift detection tooling deployed on more than 70% of estate. Alerts generated on deviation.
rubric.level4: Drift detected and alerted within 1 hour on more than 90% of estate. Auto-remediation for common deviations.
rubric.level5: Real-time drift detection across 100% of estate. Auto-remediation within minutes. Full audit trail.

parameters.name: CVE Remediation Rate by Severity
parameters.definition: % of identified CVEs remediated within the defined SLA per severity tier across the Linux server estate.

rubric.level1: No vulnerability scanning. CVEs unknown. Patching done only in response to breaches.
rubric.level2: Ad hoc scanning. CVEs identified but remediation unstructured. Critical CVEs take more than 30 days to fix.
rubric.level3: Scanning automated. SLAs defined (Critical 14 days, High 30 days). Tracked but inconsistently met.
rubric.level4: SLAs consistently met. Exception process exists. Vulnerability aging tracked and reported monthly.
rubric.level5: Critical CVEs remediated within 72 hours. Fully automated scan-to-patch pipeline. Zero unmitigated criticals.

parameters.name: Supported Kernel Version Coverage
parameters.definition: % of Linux servers running a kernel version within the vendor-supported lifecycle such as RHEL, Ubuntu LTS, or SUSE.

rubric.level1: Kernel versions not tracked. Multiple EOL kernels in production.
rubric.level2: Kernel inventory exists but more than 20% on unsupported versions. No upgrade roadmap.
rubric.level3: Inventory maintained. Upgrade plan in place. Between 5-20% on unsupported kernels.
rubric.level4: Below 5% on unsupported kernels. Lifecycle tracked per distro. Kernel upgrade process defined.
rubric.level5: 100% on supported kernels. Automated lifecycle tracking. Kernel upgrades integrated in patch pipeline.

parameters.name: Patch Cadence Compliance
parameters.definition: Adherence to the defined patching schedule per Linux distribution, measured as % of servers patched on time.

rubric.level1: No patching schedule. Servers patched only after security incidents.
rubric.level2: Patching schedule exists but less than 60% of servers patched on time. Manual process.
rubric.level3: Between 60-85% of servers patched per schedule. Yum or APT automation partially deployed.
rubric.level4: Between 85-95% of servers patched per schedule. Automated with Ansible, Satellite, or Landscape.
rubric.level5: More than 95% on-time compliance. Fully automated per distro. Staged rollout with health checks.

parameters.name: CIS Linux Benchmark Score
parameters.definition: % of CIS Benchmark controls for the relevant Linux distribution passing across the managed estate, assessed via automated tooling such as OpenSCAP, Tenable, or Qualys.

rubric.level1: No hardening baseline. Default OS configurations in production.
rubric.level2: Some hardening applied manually. No formal benchmark. Score below 50%.
rubric.level3: CIS benchmark adopted. Automated scanning in place. Score between 50-75%.
rubric.level4: Score between 75-90%. Exceptions documented with risk acceptance. Integrated in build pipeline.
rubric.level5: Score above 90%. Benchmark enforced in golden image. Continuous drift monitoring.

parameters.name: SELinux and AppArmor Enforcement
parameters.definition: % of Linux servers with SELinux on RHEL or AppArmor on Ubuntu running in Enforcing mode rather than Permissive or Disabled.

rubric.level1: SELinux or AppArmor disabled on most systems. Security modules bypassed.
rubric.level2: Modules installed but running in Permissive mode on most systems. Not enforced.
rubric.level3: Enforcing mode on more than 60% of servers. Exceptions tracked. Policies periodically reviewed.
rubric.level4: Enforcing mode on more than 90% of servers. Custom policies where needed. Alerts on violations.
rubric.level5: 100% enforcement. Custom policies managed as code. Automated violation detection and response.

parameters.name: SSH Security Hygiene
parameters.definition: Adherence to SSH security best practices including root login disabled, key-based auth enforced, idle timeout set, protocol version 2 only, and regular key rotation.

rubric.level1: Root SSH login enabled. Password authentication allowed. No key rotation policy.
rubric.level2: Some controls applied such as no root login but key rotation and idle timeout not enforced.
rubric.level3: Core SSH controls enforced via configuration management. Key rotation process defined.
rubric.level4: More than 90% of servers fully compliant with SSH policy. Automated compliance checks.
rubric.level5: 100% SSH policy compliance. SSH keys managed via PAM or vault. Auto-rotation. Full access audit trail.

parameters.name: Centralised Audit Logging (auditd)
parameters.definition: % of Linux servers with auditd configured and forwarding logs to a centralised SIEM, covering key events such as auth, privilege escalation, file access, and network connections.

rubric.level1: auditd not deployed. No central log collection from Linux systems.
rubric.level2: auditd installed on some servers. Logs stored locally only. Not centralised.
rubric.level3: auditd deployed on more than 70% of servers. Logs forwarded to central syslog or SIEM.
rubric.level4: More than 95% coverage. Audit rules tuned to capture key security events. Alerts configured.
rubric.level5: 100% coverage with enriched audit rules. SIEM correlated. Automated anomaly detection.

parameters.name: Centralised Authentication Coverage
parameters.definition: % of Linux servers authenticating users via a centralised identity provider such as Active Directory via SSSD, FreeIPA, or LDAP rather than local accounts.

rubric.level1: All authentication via local accounts. No centralised IAM for Linux.
rubric.level2: Centralised auth partially deployed. More than 30% of servers still on local-only accounts.
rubric.level3: Centralised auth on more than 70% of servers. Local accounts documented and minimised.
rubric.level4: More than 95% of servers use centralised auth. Local accounts limited to break-glass only.
rubric.level5: 100% centralised auth. Break-glass accounts vaulted in PAM. Full joiners, movers, leavers integration.

parameters.name: System Uptime and Availability
parameters.definition: % of scheduled uptime during which Linux servers are available and fully operational, excluding planned maintenance.

rubric.level1: No uptime monitoring. Availability unknown. Outages discovered by users.
rubric.level2: Basic ICMP monitoring. Approximately 95% availability. No SLA. Reactive incident management.
rubric.level3: Agent-based monitoring via Nagios, Zabbix, or Prometheus. Availability tracked versus SLA. Targeting 99%.
rubric.level4: 99.5% availability. Automated alerting and on-call integration. Capacity planning active.
rubric.level5: 99.9% or higher availability. Predictive monitoring. Automated failover. Proactive capacity management.

parameters.name: NTP Synchronisation Compliance
parameters.definition: % of Linux servers synchronised to an authoritative NTP source, with time drift within acceptable thresholds of less than 1 second.

rubric.level1: No NTP policy. Servers use default or no NTP. Time drift is common and unmonitored.
rubric.level2: NTP configured on most servers but not monitored. Drift detected reactively.
rubric.level3: NTP compliance tracked. More than 85% of servers within drift threshold. Alerts on failures.
rubric.level4: More than 98% NTP compliance. Monitoring automated. Drift alerts trigger auto-remediation.
rubric.level5: 100% NTP compliance. Chrony or NTPsec enforced via configuration management. Zero drift incidents.

parameters.name: IaC and Config Management Coverage
parameters.definition: % of Linux servers managed via Infrastructure-as-Code or configuration management tools such as Ansible, Puppet, Chef, or Salt, ensuring consistent and auditable configuration.

rubric.level1: All servers built and managed manually. No configuration management tooling.
rubric.level2: Configuration management tools deployed but used inconsistently. Less than 40% of estate managed.
rubric.level3: Between 40-75% of estate managed via IaC. Playbooks or modules for common tasks.
rubric.level4: Between 75-95% managed via IaC. Drift detection integrated. Changes via code review pipeline.
rubric.level5: More than 95% managed via IaC. Immutable infrastructure model. GitOps workflow. Full audit trail.

parameters.name: Configuration Drift Rate
parameters.definition: % of Linux servers whose actual configuration deviates from the approved IaC-defined baseline at any given time.

rubric.level1: No baseline defined. Configuration state is unknown.
rubric.level2: Baseline documented but drift not measured. Manual periodic audits only.
rubric.level3: Drift monitored on more than 70% of estate. Reports generated. Remediation is manual.
rubric.level4: Drift detected automatically. Below 5% drift rate. Auto-remediation for approved deviations.
rubric.level5: Below 1% drift rate. Real-time detection. Auto-remediation within minutes. Full change audit log.

parameters.name: Log Centralisation Coverage
parameters.definition: % of Linux servers forwarding system, application, and security logs to a centralised logging platform such as a SIEM, ELK stack, or Splunk.

rubric.level1: No central log collection. Logs stored locally only. No visibility.
rubric.level2: Less than 60% of servers forwarding logs. Coverage inconsistent. Log format not standardised.
rubric.level3: Between 60-85% of servers centralised. Common log format adopted. Basic alerting in place.
rubric.level4: More than 95% log centralisation. Log retention policy enforced. Alerting rules defined.
rubric.level5: 100% centralisation. Structured logging. Real-time correlation. SIEM fully integrated.

parameters.name: Backup Coverage and Recovery Testing
parameters.definition: % of Linux servers included in a backup schedule, combined with frequency of successful recovery tests validating restore capability.

rubric.level1: No backup policy for Linux servers. Data loss risk unmanaged.
rubric.level2: Backups configured but not monitored. Recovery never tested. Less than 80% of servers covered.
rubric.level3: Backup coverage above 85%. Success rate monitored. Recovery tested once per year.
rubric.level4: Coverage above 98%. Backup success rate above 98%. Recovery tested quarterly. RTO and RPO defined.
rubric.level5: More than 99% coverage. Automated recovery validation. Immutable backups. RTO and RPO tested monthly.

parameters.name: Cluster CPU Utilisation
parameters.definition: Average CPU utilisation across all hosts in each vSphere cluster as a % of total available CPU capacity. High utilisation risks performance degradation and reduces headroom for HA failover.

rubric.level1: No capacity monitoring. CPU utilisation unknown. VMs frequently competing for resources.
rubric.level2: Basic monitoring in place. Average utilisation often above 80%. No capacity planning.
rubric.level3: CPU utilisation tracked. Average between 60-80%. Alerts configured. Quarterly capacity review.
rubric.level4: Average CPU below 70%. DRS automation balanced across hosts. Proactive capacity planning.
rubric.level5: Average CPU below 60%. Predictive capacity management. DRS fully automated. Zero resource contention incidents.

parameters.name: vCPU to pCPU Ratio
parameters.definition: The ratio of virtual CPUs allocated to VMs versus physical CPU cores available per cluster. Over-subscription impacts performance under load.

rubric.level1: Ratio unknown. No governance on VM sizing. Significant over-commitment present.
rubric.level2: Ratio tracked per cluster but frequently exceeds 8:1. Performance issues common under load.
rubric.level3: Ratio maintained at or below 6:1 for most clusters. VM sizing guidelines exist.
rubric.level4: Ratio at or below 4:1 for production clusters. Right-sizing reviews conducted. Alerts on breach.
rubric.level5: Ratio at or below 3:1 for critical workloads. Automated right-sizing recommendations. VM sizing enforced via policy.

parameters.name: Memory Balloon and Swap Activity Rate
parameters.definition: Frequency and magnitude of VMware memory reclamation techniques being invoked, indicating memory pressure across the cluster.

rubric.level1: Memory pressure events frequent. No monitoring. VMs experience significant performance degradation.
rubric.level2: Ballooning events occur regularly. Monitored reactively. No proactive response.
rubric.level3: Ballooning events tracked and alerted. Proactive memory additions when thresholds are breached.
rubric.level4: Ballooning rare, fewer than 5 events per month per cluster. Memory headroom maintained. Automated alerts.
rubric.level5: Zero ballooning or swap events. Predictive memory management. Resource pools enforce isolation.

parameters.name: Storage Latency KPIs
parameters.definition: Average read and write latency experienced by VMs, measured at the datastore or vSAN level. Targets are read below 10ms and write below 5ms for production workloads.

rubric.level1: Storage latency not monitored. Performance issues reported by end users. No baseline established.
rubric.level2: Basic latency monitoring. Latency often exceeds 20ms. No SLA defined. Reactive response only.
rubric.level3: Latency monitored per datastore. SLA defined. Average read below 15ms, write below 10ms.
rubric.level4: Latency consistently at read below 10ms and write below 5ms. Alerts trigger capacity review.
rubric.level5: Read below 5ms, write below 2ms. Predictive I/O analytics. Automated tiering. Zero latency incidents.

parameters.name: HA Admission Control Compliance
parameters.definition: % of vSphere clusters with HA Admission Control enabled and configured to reserve sufficient resources to tolerate at least one host failure without violating VM restart guarantees.

rubric.level1: HA not configured or disabled on most clusters. Single points of failure unmanaged.
rubric.level2: HA enabled but Admission Control not configured. No guarantee of failover capacity.
rubric.level3: HA with Admission Control enabled on all production clusters. Tolerance set for 1 host failure.
rubric.level4: HA and Admission Control configured for N+1 or N+2 tolerance. Tested annually. Alerts on policy drift.
rubric.level5: HA tested quarterly via simulated host failures. N+2 for critical clusters. Automated compliance validation.

parameters.name: Snapshot Age and Sprawl
parameters.definition: Tracking of VM snapshots older than 72 hours, which risk delta disk growth, performance degradation, and excessive storage consumption.

rubric.level1: Snapshots created with no lifecycle policy. Snapshots weeks or months old are common.
rubric.level2: Snapshot age not routinely monitored. Ad hoc cleanup. Snapshots frequently exceed 7 days.
rubric.level3: Snapshot report generated weekly. Snapshots exceeding 72 hours are flagged. Manual cleanup process.
rubric.level4: Automated alerts on snapshots exceeding 24 hours. Auto-delete policy for snapshots over 72 hours in non-production.
rubric.level5: Zero snapshots older than 72 hours in production. Automated lifecycle management. Snapshot usage audited daily.

parameters.name: RPO and RTO Compliance for Protected VMs
parameters.definition: % of VMs covered by a defined backup or replication policy that meets the agreed Recovery Point Objective and Recovery Time Objective for their service tier.

rubric.level1: No RPO or RTO defined for VMs. No protection policy. Recovery capability unknown.
rubric.level2: RPO and RTO defined informally for some VMs. Coverage below 60%. Recovery never tested.
rubric.level3: RPO and RTO defined for more than 75% of VMs by service tier. Backups monitored. Annual DR test.
rubric.level4: More than 95% of VMs covered. SLA compliance reported monthly. DR tested twice yearly.
rubric.level5: 100% of VMs covered. RPO and RTO validated continuously via automated recovery testing. Real-time SLA dashboard.

parameters.name: ESXi Host Patch Level Compliance
parameters.definition: % of ESXi hosts running patch levels within the approved patching SLA, assessed against VMware published release cadence and security advisory bulletins.

rubric.level1: ESXi hosts rarely patched. Patch level unknown for most hosts. No formal process.
rubric.level2: Patching occurs but inconsistently. Many hosts more than 6 months behind. No SLA defined.
rubric.level3: Patch SLA defined. ESXi patched via Update Manager. More than 75% compliant.
rubric.level4: More than 90% of ESXi hosts within patch SLA. Baseline profiles applied. Exceptions tracked.
rubric.level5: 100% compliance. Lifecycle Manager automates ESXi updates. Patches tested in staging first.

parameters.name: vCenter MFA Enforcement
parameters.definition: Whether multi-factor authentication is enforced for all administrative access to vCenter Server and associated management interfaces via Identity Federation, Okta, or AD FS.

rubric.level1: Single-factor password-only authentication for vCenter admin access.
rubric.level2: MFA available but optional. Most administrators use password only. No enforcement.
rubric.level3: MFA enforced for privileged and admin accounts. Standard monitoring accounts exempt.
rubric.level4: MFA enforced for all accounts with write access. Identity federation configured.
rubric.level5: MFA enforced for all accounts including read-only. Phishing-resistant methods enforced. Privileged access via PAM vault.

parameters.name: VM Sprawl Rate
parameters.definition: % of VMs that are powered off for more than 30 days or are orphaned and not associated with an active workload, representing wasted resources and potential security risk.

rubric.level1: No VM lifecycle management. Large number of powered-off and orphaned VMs. No tracking.
rubric.level2: VM inventory exists but sprawl not tracked. More than 20% of VMs inactive. Cleanup ad hoc.
rubric.level3: Sprawl report generated monthly. VMs powered off for more than 30 days are flagged. Cleanup process defined.
rubric.level4: Sprawl tracked continuously. Less than 5% inactive VMs. Automated alerts trigger review workflow.
rubric.level5: Less than 2% inactive VMs. Automated decommission workflow. VM lifecycle fully governed.

parameters.name: Datastore Utilisation
parameters.definition: % of capacity used across all datastores, with a target of maintaining below 80% to ensure performance and room for snapshot and temporary file growth.

rubric.level1: Datastore utilisation not monitored. Full datastore events common. Reactive management.
rubric.level2: Utilisation checked manually. Datastores frequently exceed 85%. No automated alerts.
rubric.level3: Utilisation monitored with alerts at 80%. Monthly capacity review. Manual remediation.
rubric.level4: Alerts at 75%. Automated capacity reporting. Storage provisioning triggered proactively.
rubric.level5: Utilisation maintained below 70%. Predictive analytics. Automated tiering and expansion. Zero datastore full events.

parameters.name: VMware Tools Currency
parameters.definition: % of VMs running a current and supported version of VMware Tools, which is critical for performance and security guest OS visibility.

rubric.level1: VMware Tools not managed. Many VMs running outdated or missing Tools.
rubric.level2: Tools version tracked but update process manual and infrequent. More than 30% outdated.
rubric.level3: Tools updated during maintenance windows. More than 80% running supported versions.
rubric.level4: More than 95% running current Tools. Automated update via vCenter policy. Exceptions tracked.
rubric.level5: 100% current Tools. Automated update at VM power-on. Compliance enforced via policy.

parameters.name: Change Success Rate
parameters.definition: % of vSphere infrastructure changes that complete successfully without causing unplanned outages or rollbacks.

rubric.level1: No formal change process. Changes made ad hoc. Frequent outages caused by changes.
rubric.level2: Change process defined but inconsistently followed. Success rate below 85%. Limited testing.
rubric.level3: Change process followed for major changes. Success rate between 85-92%. Post-change reviews performed.
rubric.level4: Success rate above 95%. Pre-change testing in non-production. Automated rollback for failures.
rubric.level5: More than 99% success rate. All changes follow automated pipeline. Pre and post validation automated.

parameters.name: vMotion and Storage vMotion Success Rate & Performance
parameters.definition: Metric definition: Percentage of vMotion and Storage vMotion operations that complete successfully without errors or manual intervention, combined with average migration duration and stun time. How measured: (Successful migrations / Total attempted migrations) x 100.

rubric.level1: <80% success rate. Frequent failures or timeouts; no dedicated vMotion network. Average duration >10 minutes.
rubric.level2: 80-90% success rate. Basic vMotion network configured; average migration time 5-10 minutes.
rubric.level3: 91-97% success rate. Dedicated vMotion vmkernel ports with at least 10 GbE; average vMotion duration <3 minutes.
rubric.level4: 98-99.5% success rate. Multi-NIC vMotion with load balancing and jumbo frames; pre-flight checks in place.
rubric.level5: >=99.5% success rate with zero unplanned failures. Predictive scheduling and advanced techniques.

parameters.name: Network Configuration Compliance and Health
parameters.definition: Metric definition: Percentage of ESXi hosts, Distributed Switches, and port groups that comply with standardized networking baselines, combined with network utilization, latency, and packet drop rates.

rubric.level1: <60% compliance. Frequent configuration drift; high utilization (>90%) or latency (>10 ms); packet drops common.
rubric.level2: 60-80% compliance. Utilization often exceeds 80%; vMotion latency 5-10 ms; basic alerts configured.
rubric.level3: 81-95% compliance. All production clusters use vDS; peak utilization <70%; vMotion latency <5 ms.
rubric.level4: 96-99% compliance. Uniform vDS policies, jumbo frames, and QoS enforced; utilization <60%; latency <2 ms.
rubric.level5: 100% compliance with zero drift. Utilization proactively managed; predictive analytics for congestion.

parameters.name: Percentage of Routine Operational Tasks Automated
parameters.definition: Metric definition: Percentage of recurring operational tasks (VM provisioning, patching, snapshot cleanup, compliance checks, reporting, resource reclamation) that are fully automated with no manual intervention required.

rubric.level1: <15% automated. Most tasks performed manually or with one-off scripts; no central process.
rubric.level2: 15-40% automated. Basic PowerCLI or shell scripts used for some tasks; limited scheduling.
rubric.level3: 41-70% automated. Standard scripts and workflows exist in a central repository; scheduled via vSphere Lifecycle Manager.
rubric.level4: 71-90% automated. Policy-driven workflows using Aria Automation / Orchestrator; integrated with approval processes.
rubric.level5: >90% automated. Self-service catalog, event-driven automation, and predictive capabilities.

parameters.name: Automation Success Rate and Tool Adoption
parameters.definition: Metric definition: Combined measure of (a) success rate of automated workflows/changes and (b) percentage of operational workflows executed through formal orchestration tools (Aria Automation, vRealize Orchestrator, Ansible, Terraform).

rubric.level1: Success rate <75% and tool adoption <20%. Frequent manual interventions; orchestration rarely used.
rubric.level2: Success rate 75-88% and tool adoption 20-45%. Basic retry logic; orchestration tool used sporadically.
rubric.level3: Success rate 89-95% and tool adoption 46-70%. Standardized workflows with logging and rollback.
rubric.level4: Success rate 96-99% and tool adoption 71-90%. Automated rollback, pre-flight validation, and governance policies.
rubric.level5: Success rate >=99% and tool adoption >90%. Predictive validation, full self-service integration with ITSM/CMDB.

parameters.name: Session Launch Success Rate
parameters.definition: % of Citrix virtual app or desktop session launch attempts that succeed without error, measured across all delivery groups and Delivery Controllers.

rubric.level1: Launch success not tracked. Users report failures frequently. No visibility.
rubric.level2: Launch success tracked manually. Rate below 90%. Failures investigated only after escalation.
rubric.level3: Launch success monitored via Director. Rate between 90-97%. Alerts on failure spikes.
rubric.level4: Rate above 97%. Automated alerting. Failure patterns analysed. Root cause analysis for recurring issues.
rubric.level5: More than 99% success rate. Predictive monitoring. Auto-recovery of failed VDAs. Real-time Director dashboards.

parameters.name: Logon Time (End-to-End)
parameters.definition: Total elapsed time from a user initiating a Citrix session to reaching a usable desktop or application, including authentication, profile load, and GPO processing.

rubric.level1: Logon times not measured. Users frequently complain of slow logons. No baseline established.
rubric.level2: Logon times occasionally measured. Average exceeds 120 seconds. No optimisation effort.
rubric.level3: Logon time monitored. Average between 60-120 seconds. Profile and GPO optimisation in progress.
rubric.level4: Average logon below 60 seconds. Profile solution optimised using FSLogix or UPM. GPOs streamlined.
rubric.level5: Average logon below 30 seconds. Fully optimised. Synthetic transaction monitoring. Proactive alerting on degradation.

parameters.name: ICA Round Trip Time
parameters.definition: The time in milliseconds for a round-trip of ICA protocol packets between the client and VDA, a primary indicator of perceived session responsiveness. Target is below 150ms.

rubric.level1: ICA RTT not monitored. User experience complaints not correlated with network metrics.
rubric.level2: RTT monitored ad hoc. RTT often exceeds 300ms. No SLA. Users report poor performance.
rubric.level3: RTT monitored via Director or Analytics. Average below 200ms for most users. Alerts configured.
rubric.level4: Average RTT below 150ms. Alerts trigger network review. Branch optimisation applied.
rubric.level5: Average RTT below 100ms. HDX adaptive transport optimised. SD-WAN integrated. Per-user SLA reporting.

parameters.name: Session Reliability Event Rate
parameters.definition: Frequency of ICA session reliability auto-reconnection events occurring due to network interruptions, measured per 1000 active sessions per day.

rubric.level1: Session reliability events not tracked. Users experience frequent disconnections.
rubric.level2: Events tracked reactively. More than 10 events per 1000 sessions per day. Root cause unknown.
rubric.level3: Events tracked via Director. Between 5-10 per 1000 sessions per day. Network issues identified.
rubric.level4: Fewer than 5 events per 1000 sessions per day. Network remediation is proactive. Trend reporting in place.
rubric.level5: Fewer than 1 event per 1000 sessions per day. Predictive network analytics. Zero disconnection SLA for critical users.

parameters.name: VDA Registration Rate
parameters.definition: % of Virtual Delivery Agents that are successfully registered with a Delivery Controller and available to accept user sessions at any given time.

rubric.level1: VDA registration not monitored. Unregistered VDAs discovered only when users report failures.
rubric.level2: Registration monitored manually. Rate below 90%. Unregistered VDAs not auto-remediated.
rubric.level3: Registration rate tracked in Director. Above 93%. Alerts on unregistered VDAs.
rubric.level4: Registration rate above 97%. Auto-remediation attempted on unregistered VDAs. Daily reporting.
rubric.level5: More than 99% registration rate. Automated self-healing. Root cause auto-diagnosed. Zero user impact.

parameters.name: Delivery Controller Availability
parameters.definition: % uptime of Citrix Delivery Controllers across all sites, which are the management and session brokering layer for the Citrix estate.

rubric.level1: No monitoring of Delivery Controller health. Failures discovered by users.
rubric.level2: Basic ping monitoring. Single Delivery Controller per site with no redundancy. Downtime exceeds 0.5%.
rubric.level3: Redundant Delivery Controllers per site. Availability monitored. Targeting 99.9%.
rubric.level4: 99.9% availability. Automated failover tested. Health checks integrated with ITSM.
rubric.level5: 99.99% availability. Active-active configuration. Auto-failover. Synthetic transactions validate health.

parameters.name: StoreFront Availability
parameters.definition: % uptime of Citrix StoreFront servers, which serve the web or application portal through which users launch virtual apps and desktops.

rubric.level1: StoreFront availability not monitored. Single StoreFront with no redundancy.
rubric.level2: Storefront monitored via basic checks. Downtime events occur monthly. No redundancy.
rubric.level3: Redundant StoreFront servers deployed. Load balanced. Availability above 99%.
rubric.level4: More than 99.5% availability. Synthetic logon tests run every 5 minutes. Alerting integrated.
rubric.level5: 99.99% availability. Multi-site StoreFront with GSLB. Automated failover. Zero user-impacting outages.

parameters.name: Netscaler Availability
parameters.definition: % uptime of Citrix Netscaler devices, which external users use as a gateway to launch virtual apps and desktops.

rubric.level1: Netscaler availability not monitored. Single Netscaler with no redundancy.
rubric.level2: Netscaler monitored via basic checks. Downtime events occur monthly. No redundancy.
rubric.level3: Redundant Netscalers deployed. Load balanced. Availability above 99%.
rubric.level4: More than 99.5% availability. Synthetic logon tests run every 5 minutes. Alerting integrated.
rubric.level5: 99.99% availability. Automated failover with HA setup. Zero user-impacting outages.

parameters.name: Concurrent Session Headroom
parameters.definition: Available capacity headroom for concurrent user sessions above the observed peak load, expressed as a % buffer above peak demand.

rubric.level1: Session capacity unknown. Environment regularly hits capacity limits. Users unable to connect.
rubric.level2: Capacity tracked manually. Headroom below 10% above peak. Load spikes cause failures.
rubric.level3: Session capacity monitored. Between 10-20% headroom maintained. Monthly capacity reviews.
rubric.level4: Between 20-30% headroom maintained. Automated scaling triggers. Capacity forecasting in place.
rubric.level5: More than 30% headroom. Auto-scaling via MCS or Citrix Autoscale responds to demand. Predictive scaling.

parameters.name: VDA CPU and Memory Utilisation per Session
parameters.definition: Average CPU and memory consumed per active Citrix session on each VDA, used to validate VM sizing and detect resource contention.

rubric.level1: Per-session resource utilisation not tracked. VDA sizing not optimised. Performance complaints frequent.
rubric.level2: Utilisation tracked at host level only. No per-session data. VDAs frequently exceed 85% CPU.
rubric.level3: Per-session metrics collected via Director or monitoring tool. Sizing guidelines defined.
rubric.level4: Per-session CPU below 30% and memory below 2GB on average. Right-sizing reviews quarterly.
rubric.level5: Automated right-sizing recommendations. Per-session SLAs enforced. Anomalous sessions auto-terminated.

parameters.name: VDA OS and Citrix Version Compliance
parameters.definition: % of Virtual Delivery Agents running an OS version and Citrix VDA software version within supported lifecycle and within the approved patch currency window.

rubric.level1: VDA versions not tracked. Mix of EOL OS and outdated Citrix versions in production.
rubric.level2: Version inventory exists but more than 20% of VDAs on unsupported or EOL versions. No roadmap.
rubric.level3: Inventory maintained. Patch currency tracked. Between 5-20% behind. Upgrade plan in place.
rubric.level4: Less than 5% on unsupported versions. Patch pipeline automates VDA updates via MCS image refresh.
rubric.level5: 100% on supported versions. Image refresh automated. Zero EOL VDAs. Compliance dashboards in real time.

parameters.name: Session Recording Coverage
parameters.definition: % of privileged user, high-risk application, and regulated-environment Citrix sessions recorded via Citrix Session Recording for audit and forensic purposes.

rubric.level1: No session recording. No audit trail of user activity within Citrix sessions.
rubric.level2: Session recording deployed but used only for incident investigation. No formal policy.
rubric.level3: Recording policy defined for privileged users. More than 60% of target sessions recorded.
rubric.level4: More than 90% of defined high-risk sessions recorded. Recordings indexed and searchable.
rubric.level5: 100% coverage for all defined policies. AI-based activity detection. Forensic-grade storage.

parameters.name: Endpoint Analysis Policy Enforcement
parameters.definition: % of Citrix remote access connections subject to Endpoint Analysis scans validating device compliance such as AV status, OS patch level, and domain membership before granting session access.

rubric.level1: No EPA configured. All devices can connect regardless of security posture.
rubric.level2: EPA deployed but not enforced. Scan results not used to control access.
rubric.level3: EPA enforced for external and remote connections. Non-compliant devices restricted to quarantine.
rubric.level4: EPA enforced for all connections. Policies updated to match current compliance requirements.
rubric.level5: EPA enforced with adaptive access. Non-compliant devices auto-remediated or blocked. Logs feed SIEM.

parameters.name: Profile Load Time
parameters.definition: Time taken to load a user profile including FSLogix container mount or UPM profile sync as part of the overall logon process. Target is below 15 seconds for the profile loading component.

rubric.level1: Profile load time not measured. Profiles bloated and unmanaged. Logon storms common.
rubric.level2: Profile load often exceeds 60 seconds. No size limits. Profiles stored on overloaded file servers.
rubric.level3: Profile load between 15-60 seconds. FSLogix or UPM deployed. Basic size limits enforced.
rubric.level4: Profile load below 15 seconds. FSLogix ODFC containers on high-performance storage.
rubric.level5: Profile load below 5 seconds. Containers on NVMe or all-flash storage. Pre-load technology. Zero profile corruption.

parameters.name: FSLogix and Profile Container Health
parameters.definition: % of FSLogix profile or Office Container attach operations that succeed without error, and % of containers within defined size limits.

rubric.level1: FSLogix not deployed. Roaming profiles or no profiles in use. Frequent corruption.
rubric.level2: FSLogix deployed but not monitored. Container attach failures occur daily. No size limits.
rubric.level3: FSLogix health monitored. Attach success rate above 90%. Size alerts configured.
rubric.level4: Attach success above 97%. Sizes within policy. Failed attaches auto-remediated.
rubric.level5: More than 99% attach success. Automated container health checks. Bloated containers auto-alerted. Zero data loss.

parameters.name: Golden Image Currency
parameters.definition: Age and patch state of the Citrix master image used to provision VDAs via MCS or PVS, measured by time since last update and patch coverage.

rubric.level1: No golden image process. VDAs built manually. Images months out of date.
rubric.level2: Golden image updated infrequently, more than 3 months old. Manual update process. Testing minimal.
rubric.level3: Image updated monthly. Patches included. Basic functional testing before deployment.
rubric.level4: Image updated with each patch cycle. Automated build pipeline. Smoke tests run pre-deployment.
rubric.level5: Image fully automated. CI/CD pipeline builds, patches, tests, and deploys images. Zero manual steps.

parameters.name: Power Management Policy Compliance
parameters.definition: % of non-persistent VDA machines governed by Citrix Autoscale or equivalent power management policies, ensuring machines are drained and shut down during off-peak hours to reduce infrastructure costs.

rubric.level1: No power management. All VDAs powered on 24/7. Significant resource and cost waste.
rubric.level2: Power management partially configured. Many VDAs run overnight unnecessarily.
rubric.level3: Autoscale configured for most delivery groups. Off-peak capacity reduced by more than 40%.
rubric.level4: Autoscale optimised per delivery group schedule. Cost savings tracked and reported.
rubric.level5: Autoscale with dynamic scaling. ML-based demand prediction. Cost optimisation reported monthly.

parameters.name: SSL Certificate Compliance
parameters.definition: SSL certificates are installed on the delivery controllers, storefront servers, FSLogix and Netscaler devices for secure communication.

rubric.level1: No monitoring of SSL certificates expiry and expiry alerts not configured
rubric.level2: Partial monitoring of SSL certificate expiry installed in the servers
rubric.level3: Alerts configured through monitoring tool for 75% of the servers prior to the expiration date
rubric.level4: Expiry dates are properly tracked through alerts and certificate renewal is done 30 days prior to the expiry date.
rubric.level5: Expiry dates are properly tracked through alerts for 100% of all servers and certificate renewal is done 30 days prior to the expiry date. All information documented and reported weekly.

parameters.name: Unified Management Visibility
parameters.definition: Ability to centrally monitor and manage compute, storage, and network resources within the HCI platform through a single, integrated interface.

rubric.level1: No centralized visibility, infrastructure components are managed separately with limited monitoring.
rubric.level2: Basic centralized dashboard exists, but visibility is limited and not all components are integrated.
rubric.level3: Unified management platform provides visibility across most infrastructure components with standard monitoring.
rubric.level4: Comprehensive visibility across compute, storage, and network with proactive monitoring and alerting.
rubric.level5: End-to-end visibility across environments (including hybrid/multi-site) with advanced analytics and capacity insights.

parameters.name: Lifecycle Management (LCM patching/upgrades)
parameters.definition: Ability to plan, execute, and manage software and firmware updates (hypervisor, storage, firmware, and HCI stack) in a coordinated and controlled manner across the infrastructure.

rubric.level1: Updates are performed manually and inconsistently across components with no standard process.
rubric.level2: Basic update procedures exist, but patching is still fragmented and requires multiple tools or manual coordination.
rubric.level3: Standardized patching and upgrade processes are in place with planned schedules and documented procedures.
rubric.level4: Upgrades are centrally managed and coordinated across the HCI stack with minimal disruption and consistent execution.
rubric.level5: Lifecycle management is streamlined and regularly executed with minimal downtime, ensuring systems remain up-to-date and stable.

parameters.name: Operational Efficiency
parameters.definition: Effectiveness of managing and operating HCI infrastructure in terms of time, effort, resource utilization, and consistency of execution.

rubric.level1: Operations are manual, time-consuming, and inconsistent, leading to frequent delays and inefficiencies.
rubric.level2: Some processes are streamlined, but operations still require significant manual effort and coordination.
rubric.level3: Standard operating procedures are established, improving consistency but still dependent on manual execution.
rubric.level4: Operations are efficient with reduced manual effort, supported by standardized processes and better resource utilization.
rubric.level5: Operations are highly efficient with minimal overhead, continuously improved to maximize productivity and performance.

parameters.name: Capacity Planning (real-time vs reactive)
parameters.definition: Ability to monitor, forecast, and plan infrastructure capacity using real-time and historical data, ensuring resources are available proactively rather than reacting to shortages.

rubric.level1: No capacity planning, resources are added only after performance issues or shortages occur.
rubric.level2: Basic capacity tracking exists, but planning is reactive and based on limited or manual data.
rubric.level3: Capacity planning is performed periodically using historical trends, with defined thresholds for key resources.
rubric.level4: Capacity is continuously monitored with alerts and proactive planning aligned to growth and demand patterns.
rubric.level5: Capacity planning is integrated into operations using real-time insights, ensuring timely scaling and efficient resource utilization.

parameters.name: Scaling & Performance Predictability
parameters.definition: Ability of the HCI infrastructure to deliver consistent and predictable improvements in performance and capacity when resources (nodes, storage, compute) are added, without introducing bottlenecks.

rubric.level1: Scaling is unplanned, adding resources does not consistently improve performance and may create bottlenecks.
rubric.level2: Basic scaling is possible, but performance gains are inconsistent due to configuration or architectural limitations.
rubric.level3: Scaling processes are defined, capacity increases are predictable, but performance improvements vary across workloads.
rubric.level4: Scaling is tested and predictable, adding resources improves both capacity and performance for most workloads.
rubric.level5: Scaling consistently delivers expected performance gains across workloads with minimal bottlenecks.

parameters.name: Resource Utilization (CPU, RAM, Storage)
parameters.definition: Effectiveness of utilizing compute and storage resources within the HCI environment to balance performance and capacity without over- or under-provisioning.

rubric.level1: No visibility into resource usage, frequent over- or under-provisioning leads to inefficiency and performance issues.
rubric.level2: Basic utilization monitoring exists, but resource allocation is not optimized and often manually adjusted.
rubric.level3: Utilization is monitored with defined thresholds, resources are allocated based on standard practices, but not fully optimized.
rubric.level4: Resources are efficiently utilized with proactive monitoring and adjustments to balance performance and capacity.
rubric.level5: Resource utilization is continuously optimized based on workload needs, maximizing efficiency while maintaining performance.

parameters.name: Native Data Protection (snapshots, replication)
parameters.definition: Ability of the HCI platform to protect data using built-in features such as snapshots and replication (local and remote) to ensure data availability and recoverability.

rubric.level1: No consistent use of native data protection features, reliance is mainly on external backups.
rubric.level2: Basic snapshots or replication are configured for select workloads, but coverage is limited and inconsistent.
rubric.level3: Snapshots and replication are implemented for critical workloads with defined policies, but not fully standardized.
rubric.level4: Data protection features are consistently applied across workloads with regular monitoring and policy enforcement.
rubric.level5: Snapshots and replication are fully integrated into operations, providing reliable and efficient data protection across environments.

parameters.name: Backup Integration & Coverage
parameters.definition: Extent to which the HCI platform is integrated with backup solutions and the percentage of workloads consistently protected by backup policies.

rubric.level1: Backups are not consistently configured, many workloads are unprotected and integration with backup tools is minimal.
rubric.level2: Backups are implemented for critical workloads only, integration exists but coverage is partial and inconsistent.
rubric.level3: Backup solution is integrated with HCI platform, most workloads are protected with defined policies.
rubric.level4: Backup coverage is comprehensive with consistent policy enforcement and reliable integration across environments.
rubric.level5: All workloads are protected with standardized policies, backup integration is seamless and regularly validated.

parameters.name: Ransomware Protection (immutability)
parameters.definition: Ability to protect backup and snapshot data from ransomware attacks using mechanisms such as immutability, access controls, and isolated storage to ensure clean recovery.

rubric.level1: No specific ransomware protection, backups and data can be modified or deleted, making them vulnerable to attacks.
rubric.level2: Basic security controls (e.g., access restrictions) are in place, but data is still modifiable and exposed.
rubric.level3: Secure backup repositories and controlled access are implemented, but immutability is limited or not consistently enforced.
rubric.level4: Immutable backups or storage (e.g. WORM/object lock) are enabled with strict access controls to prevent modification or deletion.
rubric.level5: Immutable and/or isolated (air-gapped) backups are in place with regular validation to ensure reliable recovery from ransomware incidents.

parameters.name: DR Readiness (RPO/RTO alignment)
parameters.definition: Ability of the HCI environment to meet defined Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) and Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) through appropriate data protection replication and recovery processes.

rubric.level1: No defined RPO/RTO, recovery capabilities are unclear and not aligned with business needs.
rubric.level2: Basic RPO/RTO targets exist for some critical workloads, but are not consistently met.
rubric.level3: RPO/RTO are defined for key systems with supporting backup or replication, but execution is inconsistent.
rubric.level4: RPO/RTO targets are consistently achieved for critical workloads through tested DR processes.
rubric.level5: DR capabilities are well-aligned with business requirements, recovery is reliable and consistently meets defined RPO/RTO across environments.

parameters.name: High Availability (HA) Coverage
parameters.definition: % of production databases with automated failover and redundancy (e.g., AlwaysOn, RAC, Mirroring).

rubric.level1: HA exists for critical DBs only
rubric.level2: HA exists for critical DBs only. Manual failover required.
rubric.level3: HA standardized for all production DBs. Failover is automated but rarely tested.
rubric.level4: Multi-node/site HA with 99.9% availability. Regular failover drills performed.
rubric.level5: 99.99%+ availability. Active-Active setups. Zero-downtime maintenance and automated healing.

parameters.notes: Implement HA/DR strategy using Oracle RAC, Data Guard, or cloud-native HA capabilities to reduce single-point-of-failure risk.

parameters.name: Backup & Recovery Success Rate
parameters.definition: % of successful backups and validated restores within defined RPO/RTO.

rubric.level1: No formal backups. Success unknown. Recovery never tested.
rubric.level2: Backups run but not monitored. Success rate <85%.
rubric.level3: Backups monitored centrally. 85-95% success. Annual recovery testing.
rubric.level4: >98% success. Failures trigger auto-alerts. Quarterly recovery validation.
rubric.level5: 100% success. Automated, continuous recovery testing. Immutable backups.

parameters.notes: Backup operations are automated through scheduled scripts/tool, and recovery procedures are periodically validated during refresh activities. However, recovery execution remains manual and centralized reporting/validation can be improved.

parameters.name: Hardening & Compliance
parameters.definition: Adherence to security baselines (e.g., CIS Benchmarks) and encryption status.

rubric.level1: No hardening. Default passwords in use. No encryption.
rubric.level2: Manual hardening applied. Some encryption at rest.
rubric.level3: Standardized hardening policy. Automated scanning. Data-at-rest encryption for all.
rubric.level4: 90%+ compliance with CIS. TDE and Data-in-Transit encryption enforced.
rubric.level5: 100% compliance. Real-time drift detection. Automated masking and tokenization.

parameters.notes: Basic security controls are implemented; however, encryption standards, password governance, and centralized compliance enforcement require improvement.

parameters.name: Privileged Access Management (PAM)
parameters.definition: Management of DBA and Application account access, including MFA and least privilege.

rubric.level1: Shared sa or root passwords. No MFA. Broad access for all.
rubric.level2: Named accounts for DBAs. MFA on management plane. Periodic manual review.
rubric.level3: RBAC enforced. MFA for all privileged access. Quarterly access audits.
rubric.level4: Automated JIT (Just-in-Time) access. 95%+ MFA coverage. Integrated with PAM vault.
rubric.level5: Zero-trust model. No permanent privileged accounts. AI-based anomaly detection for DB access.

parameters.notes: Privileged access is managed through standard database authentication without MFA or enterprise PAM integration.

parameters.name: Vulnerability Management
parameters.definition: Process for scanning, identifying, and remediating DB-specific CVEs and configuration flaws.

rubric.level1: No scanning. Vulnerabilities only addressed during major upgrades or after a breach.
rubric.level2: Periodic manual scans. No formal SLA for patching critical vulnerabilities.
rubric.level3: Monthly automated vulnerability scans. Critical patches applied within 30 days.
rubric.level4: Real-time vulnerability assessment. Integrated with SOC/SIEM. 95% of DBs meet patch SLAs.
rubric.level5: Continuous zero-day protection. Automated virtual patching and instant remediation of drift.

parameters.notes: Vulnerability remediation activities are partially aligned with quarterly patching cycles; however, centralized vulnerability scanning and SLA-driven remediation require improvement.

parameters.name: Query Tuning & Analytics
parameters.definition: Monitoring of slow queries, index fragmentation, and execution plans.

rubric.level1: No monitoring. Performance issues handled reactively based on user complaints.
rubric.level2: Basic resource monitoring (CPU/Memory). Occasional manual tuning.
rubric.level3: APM/DB monitoring tools in place. Slow query logs reviewed weekly.
rubric.level4: Proactive tuning based on wait-state analysis. Automated alerts for performance degradation.
rubric.level5: AI-driven query optimization. Predictive performance analytics. Zero manual tuning required.

parameters.notes: Oracle OEM-based monitoring provides proactive visibility into database performance, query bottlenecks, and resource utilization, enabling operational performance management.

parameters.name: Patching & EOL Exposure
parameters.definition: % of DBs on supported versions and current security patch levels.

rubric.level1: No patching schedule. Many EOL versions in production.
rubric.level2: Inconsistent patching. Vulnerability remediation takes >60 days.
rubric.level4: Automated patch deployment. 95%+ compliance within 30 days of release.
rubric.level5: Zero EOL versions. Self-patching/Green-Blue deployment pipelines. Real-time compliance.

parameters.notes: Quarterly patch management processes are established and operationally maintained; however, further automation and compliance reporting opportunities exist.

parameters.name: Automated Provisioning
parameters.definition: % of DB deployments handled via IaC (Terraform, Ansible) or Self-Service Portals.

rubric.level1: Manual DB creation. Configuration varies every time.
rubric.level2: Basic scripts for installation. 50% manual effort remains.
rubric.level3: Standardized images/templates. DB-as-a-Service (DBaaS) available for Dev.
rubric.level4: 90%+ IaC coverage. Automated configuration management and drift detection.
rubric.level5: 100% automated lifecycle. GitOps workflow. Self-healing configuration.

parameters.notes: Provisioning activities are primarily manual, supported by scheduled backend scripts without Infrastructure-as-Code or orchestration framework integration.

parameters.name: Cloud & Platform Modernization
parameters.definition: Transition from legacy VM-based DBs to Cloud-Native/PaaS (RDS, Cloud SQL, Aurora) or NoSQL.

rubric.level1: Entirely on-prem legacy VMs. No cloud strategy.
rubric.level2: Some Lift & Shift to cloud VMs (IaaS). No PaaS usage.
rubric.level3: Strategy defined for PaaS adoption. 30% of non-prod on PaaS/DBaaS.
rubric.level4: 70%+ of workloads on PaaS. Significant use of NoSQL/NewSQL where applicable.
rubric.level5: 100% Cloud-Native or Serverless where possible. Multi-region/Global distribution.

parameters.notes: Cloud migration initiatives are in progress; however, migration activities remain largely manual without standardized cloud-native operational practices.

parameters.name: CI/CD Integration (Database DevOps)
parameters.definition: Integration of database schema changes into the application deployment pipeline.

rubric.level1: Manual SQL scripts run by DBAs. No version control for schemas.
rubric.level2: SQL scripts stored in Git, but deployments are still manual.
rubric.level3: Automated schema migrations (e.g., Liquibase/Flyway) in non-prod environments.
rubric.level4: Full CI/CD for DB changes in all environments. Automated rollback capability.
rubric.level5: DataOps fully realized. Self-service schema changes with automated policy guardrails.

parameters.notes: Database deployment and change management activities are currently executed manually without CI/CD pipeline integration.

parameters.name: Instance & License Density
parameters.definition: Reduction of sprawl by consolidating small DBs onto shared platforms or multi-tenant clusters.

rubric.level1: Massive sprawl; hundreds of underutilized standalone instances. High licensing waste.
rubric.level2: Initial inventory completed. Manual consolidation of dev/test environments.
rubric.level3: Multi-tenancy (e.g., SQL Instances/Oracle CDB) used for 40% of workloads.
rubric.level4: 80% consolidation achieved. Standardized T-shirt sizing for all DB deployments.
rubric.level5: Extreme density. Serverless/Elastic scaling used to eliminate idle resources. Zero ghost DBs.

parameters.notes: Database environments are primarily deployed as standalone instances without consolidation or high-density architecture optimization.

parameters.name: Self-Healing & Remediation
parameters.definition: The ability of the system to detect and fix common DB issues without human intervention.

rubric.level1: 100% manual intervention for every alert or disk-full event.
rubric.level2: Basic scripts for log truncation or service restarts.
rubric.level3: Automation library for common tasks (e.g., automated index rebuilds, disk expansion).
rubric.level4: Event-driven automation. 70% of routine alerts resolved by automated workflows.
rubric.level5: Fully autonomous. Self-healing DB clusters that scale, patch, and tune without DBA input.

parameters.notes: Operational incidents and service interruptions currently require manual intervention and remediation activities.

parameters.name: AIOps & Predictive Analytics
parameters.definition: Use of Machine Learning to predict failures, optimize performance, and manage security.

rubric.level1: No AI usage. Monitoring is purely threshold-based (e.g., alert at 90% CPU).
rubric.level2: Basic trend analysis. Using vendor-provided Advisors for query tuning.
rubric.level3: Centralized AIOps platform ingesting DB logs for anomaly detection.
rubric.level4: Predictive alerting (alerts trigger before failure). AI-driven capacity planning.
rubric.level5: Generative AI integrated for SQL generation/optimization. Autonomous DBA bots manage ops.

rubric.level3: Backup policies defined and tracked but inconsistently enforced

rubric.level5: >99% compliance with policy-driven automation.

rubric.level3: Restore testing is scheduled (e.g. quarterly/annual for key systems). Results are documented.

rubric.level2: Encryption is enabled for some backups but not consistently across all workloads.
rubric.level3: Encryption is standardized for backups but key management is basic or manually handled.

rubric.level2: Basic security controls in place (access restrictions, antivirus) but backups are still modifiable and exposed.
rubric.level3: Hardened backup repositories with limited access in Cloud/offsite backups.
rubric.level4: Immutable backups enabled with WORM/object lock enabled, separation between backup and production environments.
rubric.level5: Strict access governance in place with air-gapped backup implemented. Regular recovery testing to ensure clean restore points.
